name: CreateCollection
caption: Create Collection

configuration.description: Name of the collection. Becomes the step's single output name, so downstream steps address it as {{<slug>_<collectionName>}}. Plain text (no SmartField resolution). Use an identifier-like name (letters, digits, hyphens) because it is embedded in placeholders.
0 = Value (collection of text values), 1 = Reference (collection of record references). Missing/unknown is treated as 0 (Value) when outputs are generated.
Table number the references point to. Required when collectionType = 1; the editor writes 0 for Value collections. Copied into the output's tableNo.

rules.check: configuration.collectionName must be non-empty (required field in the config canvas; the step's validity check also fails without it). Without a name no output is generated.
rules.message: Please fill in the highlighted fields.

rules.check: configuration.collectionType must be a JSON integer.
configuration.tableNo must be a non-zero table number when collectionType = 1 (Reference).
rules.message: Please fill in the highlighted fields.

rules.check: tableNo, when given, must be a non-negative integer that is an existing table in the target environment (the table picker only offers existing tables).

notes: The step does nothing at run time: an empty collection has no runtime representation. Entries appear only when an Add to Collection step appends to it, under the names <slug>_<collectionName>[0], [1], ...
Downstream steps that iterate or aggregate over the collection reference the declared output {{<slug>_<collectionName>}}. If no item was ever added, the collection does not exist at run time.

If the Create Collection step sits inside a loop/branch body, its runtime rows are cleaned up when that body is left (rows of steps inside a closed edge are removed). Place it at the level where the collection must stay readable, typically before the loop that fills it.
The editor seeds description 'Create <collectionName> Collection' and a PascalCase slug derived from it; both may be overridden.
